text:
marta_olsen: Pushing up the Cygnus LoRA merge to rtx-serve-4bit. Merge succeeded but the quick smoke pack is failing on instruction-follow tests. Anyone seen this pattern before?

jamal_k: saw something similar when tokenizer changed during fine-tune. How big is the metric delta?

marta_olsen: instruction-follow accuracy down ~12% vs base rtx-1. Baseline pass rate was 92%, current ~80%. Hallucination rate increased on the factual QA sets.

eval-bot: smoke-eval run finished: 5 failing checks out of 48. Failures: date_parse, table_formatting, small-math, codeblock-fence, polite_rewrite. Full log: ```FAIL date_parse: expected 2023-11-12 got 2023/11/12
FAIL table_formatting: misaligned columns for 3/10 examples
FAIL small-math: 5/20 incorrect 
FAIL codeblock-fence: missing backticks in 2/5 
FAIL polite_rewrite: added irrelevant context in 4/8```

ciara: can you repro locally with hf checkpoint + merged LoRA? or is this only on rtx quantized path?

marta_olsen: repro on float32 baseline (local) -> merged LoRA float32 shows smaller drop (~3-4%), so major delta seems introduced by 4-bit quant path.

ben_p: sounds like quantization nonlinearity. Couple of checks: 1) tokenizer drift (new special tokens), 2) KV-cache alignment, 3) layernorm/epsilon mismatch when folding.

jamal_k: +1 on tokenizer. Run `python -m tools.tokenizer_inspect --base model-x --finetuned cygnus-lora` and diff tokens. If special tokens changed, quant impl sometimes remaps IDs badly.

marta_olsen: ran token diff: ```Added tokens: ['<CY_CUSTOM>']
Substitutions: none
Token id offset: 0```  so not huge, but there is one custom token the customer added.

ciara: ok, not a token-id shift then. Ben—can you try a quick run disabling KV cache and see if attention caching is a culprit?

ben_p: launching quick run on rtx-4bit with KV disabled. command: `./run_smoke.sh --model rtx-serve-4bit --no-kv --pack quick-cygnus` 

deploy-bot: queued job 8675309 on pool-rtc-4. ETA ~2m.

ben_p: interim results: disabling KV improves table_formatting and codeblock-fence, but small-math and date_parse still failing. Looks like numeric precision got hit.

marta_olsen: that suggests a mixed failure: unsafe quant for arithmetic tokens + some cache-related formatting regressions. Any quick quant patches we can try? Per-layer scale clamp?

jamal_k: try per-channel scaling and disable quant for the final few FFN layers (they're sensitive for numeric ops). I can patch runtime to keep last 2 FFN layers in fp16.

ciara: also try running int8 fallback for the math/date tests to compare. If int8 recovers metrics, it's a 4-bit specific dynamic range problem.

eval-bot: added new eval set job: `smoke-quant-compare` (int8 vs 4bit vs fp16)

ben_p: quick numbers after fp16 fallback on last2-ffn: instruction-follow up to -5% (better than -12%). small-math recovered ~75% -> 90% correct on that subset. Dates still shaky.

marta_olsen: progress. Could the fine-tune have changed EOS/stop token behavior that interacts with our post-processing? We saw polite_rewrite adding extra text earlier.

ciara: check output token sequences raw (no detokenize) for EOS usage. Might be token collision with <CY_CUSTOM> if it equals an internal sentinel.

marta_olsen: raw tokens snippet for fail case: `[1203, 4, 502, 9999, 2]` where 2 is EOS. The custom token id 9999 appears mid-output more often in failing samples.

jamal_k: that looks like the LoRA injected behavior to use the custom token as a separator. Quantizer may be aliasing it to similar embedding vector when compressed. Can we try reinitializing embedding scale for that token before quant? Quick hack: zero-out that token embedding delta and re-eval.

ben_p: applied zero-out patch to token 9999 in runtime quant prep. Re-ran smoke pack. Result: polite_rewrite fixed, table_formatting improved, instruction-follow still -6%. small-math ~88%. Dates mostly recovered.

marta_olsen: zero-out helped a lot. But we can't ship that as-is for customer — it removes their custom token semantics. Need a safer fix.

ciara: longer-term: 1) force cust tokens into FP storage (exclude from quant) 2) or teach quantizer per-token-aware scaling. For quick release, we can add a compatibility flag: `--preserve-special-tokens` that avoids quantizing specified token ids.

jamal_k: I'll prototype `--preserve-tokens 9999` in runtime. Should be low-risk.

marta_olsen: plan summary: jamal prototype preserve-tokens flag, ben keep last2-ffn fp16 fallback enabled, ciara run int8 vs 4bit full smoke to capture regression matrix. If all agree, build can be flagged for Cygnus tenant as `compat-qualifier=v1` and roll canary.

deploy-bot: canary build available: rtx-serve-4bit-compat-v1 tagged.

marta_olsen: assign: jamal -> prototype preserve-tokens (ETA 3h), ben -> perf/latency check with last2-ffn-fp16 fallback (ETA 1h), ciara -> full smoke matrix + write quick eval report for Cygnus (ETA 4h). I'll coordinate customer comms after we have matrix. :thumbsup:

ben_p: noted. If latency cost is >8% we should consider optional fallback per-route rather than global.

jamal_k: prototype done in 1.5h, tests running. sending logs if green.

marta_olsen: awesome — thanks team. We'll reconvene here when eval report is in. (reacts: :eyes:)
